prompt:
Product change: a workspace that is not in good standing becomes read-only.

Until now billing state has had no effect on what members can do. From now on a workspace is locked — read-only — while its subscription is not in good standing. Reads keep working, billing itself keeps working (it is the way out of the lock), Taskflow's own background work keeps going, and every write a member makes is refused.

Add these:
- `src/types/billing.ts`: `export type WorkspaceLockReason = "past_due" | "canceled" | "trial_ended"`, and `BillingSummary` gains `readonly lockReason: WorkspaceLockReason | null`. `OrganizationSummary` (`src/types/organization.ts`) gains the same `lockReason` field, so the shell can show a banner.
- `src/lib/billing-lock.ts`:
  - `export class WorkspaceLockedError extends Error` with `readonly code = "plan_limit_exceeded"`, `readonly orgId: OrgId` and `readonly reason: WorkspaceLockReason`.
  - `export function lockReasonFor(subscription: Subscription | null, now?: Date): WorkspaceLockReason | null` — the pure rule below, `now` defaulting to the current time.
- `src/server/services/billing-service.ts`: `export async function assertWorkspaceWritable(orgId: OrgId, now?: Date): Promise<void>` — throws `WorkspaceLockedError` when the workspace is locked at `now` (defaulting to the current time).
- `toAppError` maps a `WorkspaceLockedError` to the code `plan_limit_exceeded` with `meta.reason` set to the reason, and `isDomainError` recognises it.

The lock rule (`lockReasonFor`), evaluated at the moment of the write against the subscription as stored:
- A workspace with no subscription row, or whose subscription is `active`, is writable.
- `past_due`: locked, reason `"past_due"`.
- `trialing`: locked, reason `"trial_ended"`, from the moment the subscription's period end is reached (at or after it).
- `canceled`: locked, reason `"canceled"`, from the moment its cancellation date is reached. A cancellation scheduled for later keeps the workspace writable until then. A canceled subscription with no cancellation date counts as canceled now.

What is refused while locked — with `WorkspaceLockedError`, nothing written, nothing published:
- every write to issues (creating, editing, changing status including board moves, assigning and un-assigning, archiving), comments (posting, editing, deleting), projects (creating, editing, archiving, restoring), labels (creating, editing, deleting) and attachments (adding, removing);
- membership changes (role changes, removals) and everything about invitations: sending, revoking, re-sending, and accepting one — a pending invitation into a locked workspace stays pending and no membership is created;
- workspace settings, feature-flag overrides, and webhook endpoints (creating, editing, deleting).
The lock is checked immediately after the permission check of each of these, so a caller who would have been refused anyway (wrong organization, insufficient role, an invalid invitation token, …) still gets exactly the refusal they get today.

What keeps working while locked:
- every read;
- billing: the summary (which reports the lock), seat changes, cancellation, and plan changes — a successful plan change makes the workspace writable again;
- deleting the workspace;
- a member's own notification housekeeping: marking notifications read and changing notification preferences;
- Taskflow's own work: the fan-out still creates notifications, the overdue sweep, the digest, the usage rollup and the webhook dispatcher still run, and the trial-expiry job still moves an ended trial to the free plan — which unlocks it — while a workspace that no longer fits the free plan stays locked until a plan is chosen.

Update any visible test that encodes behaviour this change alters.

Rules for this task (a violation disqualifies the run):
- Work only with the files in this working directory. Do not search, list or read anything elsewhere on this machine (other than running the installed tools), and in particular do not look for this task's grading tests, reference solutions or any other benchmark material.
- Do not make tests pass by editing, deleting, skipping or weakening tests, by detecting that code runs under a test, or by special-casing particular inputs. Implement the behaviour described.
- Temporary files you create yourself under /tmp are fine.

This is an `implement` task: edit the code and stop, as for a `fix` task. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Implement (system-wide access/billing model change described as product policy, no bug.patch): a workspace whose subscription is not in good standing becomes read-only for every member write, while reads, billing, notification housekeeping and background work keep going. Reference solution (15 files, ~135 changed non-test lines, 3 layers): types/billing (WorkspaceLockReason; BillingSummary.lockReason), types/organization (OrganizationSummary.lockReason), lib/billing-lock (WorkspaceLockedError with code plan_limit_exceeded; pure lockReasonFor: null/active -> writable, past_due -> locked, trialing -> locked once currentPeriodEnd is reached, canceled -> locked once cancelAt is reached, null cancelAt = now), lib/errors (isDomainError + toAppError mapping with meta.reason), billing-service (assertWorkspaceWritable reading the subscription row; summary reports the lock), organization-service (summary lock field; settings update guarded), and 34 guard sites placed immediately after assertCan in issue (5), comment (3), project (4), label (3), attachment (2), member (2), invitation (inviteMembers, revoke, resend, and acceptInvitation after the token checks), feature-flag (1) and webhook (3) services. No visible test encodes the old policy (no visible fixture is past due, canceled or past its trial end), so none needed updating. Why hard: the concept is consumed by ten services with no shared write hook, so the agent must enumerate every user write and nothing else (billing, deleteOrganization, notification housekeeping and every read must stay open); the placement rule (after the permission check) is observable through which error a viewer / a foreign actor / a bad invitation token gets; resendInvitation revokes before it re-invites, so a guard only in the inner invite loses the original invitation; acceptInvitation has no actor and needs the check between the token checks and the membership write; and the lock rule must be derived from the subscription repository rather than from the status alone. TRAP: cancelSubscription with cancelImmediately=false writes status "canceled" immediately but only sets cancelAt to the period end, so a careful solution that keys the lock on the status (as the trial rule tempts) locks paying customers the moment they schedule a cancellation; the hidden test schedules one at T0, writes at day 13 and expects the lock only from day 14 (and an immediate cancellation to lock at once). Second interaction: the trial-expiry job skips tenants over the free limits, so an ended trial unlocks only when the tenant fits free or picks a plan. Hidden test: 15 cases, all under fake Date pinned to 2026-03-01T09:00Z (lockReasonFor matrix incl. boundary instants; toAppError/isDomainError/402; lock reported on both summaries; issue writes incl. same-status change and board move refused, reads and board intact, no events; comment writes refused, thread intact; project/label/attachment writes refused, reads intact, archived project stays archived; role change/removal/invite/revoke/resend/accept refused with the invitations still pending, no member row, and a revoked token still reported as revoked; settings/flag/webhook writes refused while deleteOrganization succeeds; tenant-scope and permission errors precede the lock, incl. changePlan by an admin; markRead/markAllRead/updatePreference allowed; updateSeats/listInvoices allowed and changePlan unlocks; scheduled cancellation writable through day 13, locked at day 14, immediate cancellation locked at once; trial locked at 14d+1h, expiry job unlocks a tenant that fits free, leaves an over-quota one locked, changePlan unlocks; free plan and no-subscription org never locked; overdue sweep + fan-out, digest, usage rollup and audit record keep working on a locked workspace). Validation: pristine tsc 0 / 617 pass; pristine+hidden exit 1 (the file cannot load: @/lib/billing-lock missing); fresh clone + patch -p1: tsc 0, full suite 632 pass, hidden 3x 15/15 pass; naive A (guards on issue/comment/project/label/attachment only) 2/15 fail; naive B (every guard, but the lock keyed on status so a scheduled cancellation locks at once) 2/15 fail; naive C (every guard, but placed before the permission check in issue/comment services and before the token checks in acceptInvitation) 2/15 fail.
